subject: Renewal discussion: SLA-linked credits & temporary price hold
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal prep — worried about latency spikes and costs

Hi Marissa,

Our renewal is coming up and usage has grown 3x this quarter — great news, but it also exposed a couple of problems: intermittent latency during peak jobs and some unexpectedly high overage charges on the last invoice. Before we renew, our execs want a clearer playbook on how Redwood will protect us from price surprises while we scale.

Specifically, can Redwood consider: a) a short-term price hold for the first 90 days of the renewed term while we stabilize traffic, and b) a latency-linked credit schedule (if 95p latency > 450ms, apply credits scaled to tokens processed during the window)?

We'd like to avoid committing to a materially higher fixed spend until our throughput pattern stabilizes. Legal and Ops are on this thread for the compliance/ops implications.

Can we get a proposal this week? Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Petrov

Elena — thanks for the note and congrats on the growth.

Short answer: yes, we can structure a renewal that addresses both concerns. I attached a draft term sheet and a simple SLA-credit matrix for the latency triggers you suggested. High level proposal:

- 90-day temporary price hold (hold current list rate for your committed capacity tier for first 90 days of the new term).
- Latency-linked credits: credits applied as percentage reduction on the following invoice if 95th percentile > threshold; matrix attached (example: 95p > 450ms -> 3% credit on token spend that month; 95p > 600ms -> 7% credit).
- Commit flexibility: allow one mid-term true-up window at 45 days to convert burst usage into committed capacity at a prorated rate (reduces future overage risk).
- Limited fallback: credits only apply to hosted inference consumption, not third-party infra pass-throughs.

I'll loop Karthik for the pricing mechanics and Vivek for an engineering confirmation that the latency signals and telemetry we rely on are measurable and auditable. If that looks OK from your legal side, we can prepare an amendment to the current agreement + DocuSign.

Proposed next steps: quick sync with Ops + Legal today or tomorrow, and I can send the formal amendment by EOD Thursday.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

(Attachments: OrchidSoft_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf, SLA-latency-credit-matrix.xlsx)

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Elena's ask and Marissa's draft. A few internal notes (keeping it short):

- Pricing: the 90-day price hold is acceptable if we tie it to a baseline commit (e.g., Orchid maintains at least 75% of prior quarter commit or agrees to a conservative short-term commit). Otherwise the revenue risk is too high. Suggest adding a provisional minimum commit clause for the hold period.
- Credits: engineering needs the exact metric definition. Vivek, can we guarantee the 95p latency as defined in their client-side logs vs our server-side telemetry? If not, we should specify Redwood's issuer of the metric (Redwood telemetry, with customer's log export as validation).
- True-up window: one-window approach is fine but limit to converting burst into committed units with a 30% uplift on committed discount tiers to avoid oversubscription.

If we agree, I'll draft the pricing clause language and run it with finance for expected revenue treatment. Also recommend we include a hard cap on monthly credit exposure (e.g., credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice) to limit downside.

-Karthik
